issue.title: dedupe.ts misses overlapping days when two statements are uploaded together
issue.body:
Duplicate detection in `src/ingest/dedupe.ts` doesn't handle overlapping
statements uploaded together. I uploaded our September and October statements
straight after each other; both contain 28 to 30 September, and those three
days are now in the ledger twice (both uploads say 0 duplicates). On our test
account I uploaded the same two files a few minutes apart, and the second one
reported 9 duplicates, as it should. So dedupe.ts must be missing a case.
## Discussion

### ben-ops (maintainer) · 2026-11-12
Thanks. Roughly how long was there between the two uploads, and how big are
the files?

### recon-team-milan · 2026-11-12
About ten seconds apart, around 2,000 rows each. Both had finished importing
within a minute.

input.title: Stop concurrent imports for one account from duplicating overlapping rows
input.body:
File: src/ingest/worker.ts

processJob reads the account's existing rows (listInRange) and then inserts the deduped rows (insertMany) with no coordination. startWorker runs config.queue.concurrency loops, so two uploads for the same account that are claimed together (~10s apart, both still processing) each read the ledger before the other has inserted, and both report 0 duplicates. Proposed change: make the read-dedupe-insert section run serialized per account (e.g. a per-account lock/queue around the listInRange..insertMany block, or claim jobs so only one per account runs at a time). A DB-level unique key on the dedupe key would be a stronger backstop. dedupe.ts itself is correct: it works when the second upload sees the first's rows, as the reporter's test account shows.

This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

dedupe.ts is correct: it drops rows already in the set it is given. The problem is in processJob in worker.ts. It reads the account's existing rows and then inserts, with no locking. startWorker runs several loops at once, so two uploads for the same account that are processed together both read the ledger before either has inserted, and both report 0 duplicates. That fits the 10-second gap in your report, and it fits the test account, where the later upload saw the first one's rows. I opened a draft PR (pr-25) proposing that the read, dedupe and insert steps run one at a time per account.
